title: Spark batches approved proposals into a weekly Monday governance cycle with a Friday cut-off
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.4 sets the voting mechanics: a Snapshot poll open for three days, where "a poll must have more than 50% of votes cast, excluding abstentions, in favor to be approved," and token holders may vote directly or through Delegates.

The scheduling layer is the more interesting part. "Spark's governance runs in a weekly cycle that begins every Monday. Upon receiving all approvals, the proposal is automatically included in the next cycle. The cut-off time is Friday 8:00 am UTC to ensure the Operational Facilitator has sufficient time to prepare the needed polls for the following Monday."

Batching decisions into a fixed weekly cadence buys predictability for everyone: participants know when to pay attention, and the Facilitator gets a bounded preparation window instead of a continuous queue. The counting rule — majority of votes cast excluding abstentions, with no quorum stated here — favours decidability over a mandate threshold: a poll cannot fail merely from low turnout.

One discretionary seam remains: after the cut-off, "it is at the discretion of the Operational Facilitator whether the proposal can be included in the immediate next cycle, or the following cycle." Timing power over a week's delay sits with the Facilitator, which is minor for routine edits and material for time-sensitive ones.
description: A three-day Snapshot poll needing >50% of non-abstaining votes feeds a fixed weekly cadence; proposals arriving after Friday 08:00 UTC slip at the Facilitator's discretion.
